newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker installs client logistics system.
newsitem.headline: Schenker installs client logistics system.

text.p: Global freight forwarder Schenker International AG said it will install a logistics information network for shippers and suppliers in the second half of this year.
Its logistics manager Reinhard Riss said the new Integrated Logistics System (ILS) was a key element of the company's aim to become a "super-integrator" offering full logistics services.
The ILS will cover the Schenker in-house system Sword, a new customer information system and other systems such as Traxon or customs services, he told Reuters in an interview.
Each customer will have a user profile of transport needs, can track and trace shipments directly online and monitor warehousing status, he added.
Different modules would be adapted for specific industries such as semiconductors, computer equipment and international department store purchasing.
Riss said: "With this system we can cover all our logistics solutions and services. It is a tailor-made logistics management system.
"The strength of the system is that big and small companies, whether with 10,000 or two shipments, can use it," he added.
The ILS system will be installed in Schenker offices in Asia, Europe and the Americas over the coming months with worldwide coverage by the end of 1998.

Riss, appointed Schenker International logistics manager in March 1996, explained: "Logistics has become a high priority for Schenker. We want to get away from being only a forwarder and towards being a logistics supplier or a super-integrator."
